- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.prompt:
Search this repository very thoroughly for a Markdown processing interface/abstraction. I need to find:
1. An interface (abstract class, trait, protocol, or TypeScript interface) for markdown processing/rendering
2. Concrete implementation(s) of that interface
3. Where those implementations are constructed/instantiated
4. Which components hold references to the interface type

Search for terms like "markdown", "MarkdownProcessor", "MarkdownParser", "MarkdownRenderer", "IMarkdown", etc. Look in all languages present in the repo. Check dependency injection configurations, factory methods, and constructor parameters. Report file paths and line numbers.

content.text:
I now have a complete picture. Here is my report.

---

## Markdown Processing Interface/Abstraction -- Complete Report

### 1. The Interface (Go)

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, lines 31-55

The primary markdown processing abstraction is a Go interface named `Service` in package `markdown`:

```go
type Service interface {
    ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)
    ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)
    ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)
    RenderMarkdown(content []byte) (string, error)
    RenderHTML(content []byte) (string, error)
    GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)
    ValidateContent(content []byte) error
    RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error)
}
```

There is no equivalent TypeScript interface for a markdown "processor" on the frontend. The frontend uses the `react-markdown` library directly (via the `MemoMarkdownRenderer` component) and has component-level interfaces such as `MemoMarkdownRendererProps` and `EditorController`, but no abstract markdown service contract.

---

### 2. Concrete Implementation

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, lines 57-60 (declaration), lines 85-113 (constructor)

The single concrete implementation is an unexported struct `service`:

```go
type service struct {
    md goldmark.Markdown
}
```

It is constructed by the factory function `NewService(opts ...Option) Service` at line 85. This function accepts functional options (`WithTagExtension`, `WithMentionExtension`) and configures a `goldmark.Markdown` instance with GFM extensions and optionally custom tag/mention parsing.

Additionally, there is a supporting struct `MarkdownRenderer` (not implementing the `Service` interface, but used internally by it):

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go`, lines 15-24

This is a concrete struct that renders a goldmark AST back to markdown text. It is instantiated via `NewMarkdownRenderer()` and used internally by `service.RenderMarkdown()` (line 250) and `service.RenameTag()` (line 451) in `markdown.go`.

---

### 3. Where Implementations Are Constructed/Instantiated

There are **four** instantiation sites:

| # | File | Line | Options Used |
|---|------|------|-------------|
| 1 | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` | 48-51 | `WithTagExtension()`, `WithMentionExtension()` |
| 2 | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go` | 44-46 | `WithTagExtension()`, `WithMentionExtension()` |
| 3 | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go` | 427 | `WithTagExtension()` only |
| 4 | `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss_test.go` | 54 | No options (bare `NewService()`) |

The primary production instantiation is #1, inside `NewAPIV1Service()`. The service is then **shared** with the RSS service at `/bench/repo/server/server.go`, line 85:

```go
rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)
```

---

### 4. Components That Hold References to the Interface Type

Three structs hold `markdown.Service` as a field:

| Struct | File | Line | Field Name |
|--------|------|------|-----------|
| `APIV1Service` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` | 35 | `MarkdownService markdown.Service` |
| `Runner` (memopayload) | `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` | 16 | `MarkdownService markdown.Service` |
| `RSSService` | `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go` | 45 | `MarkdownService markdown.Service` |

One standalone function also accepts the interface as a parameter:

| Function | File | Line |
|----------|------|------|
| `RebuildMemoPayload()` | `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` | 74 |

**Usage sites within `APIV1Service`** (which holds `s.MarkdownService`):

- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 108 -- calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService)` during memo creation
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 447 -- calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService)` during memo update
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go` line 32 -- calls `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll()` to resolve mention targets
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` line 85 -- calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet()` for webhook payloads

---

### 5. Frontend Markdown Rendering (TypeScript/React -- no abstract interface)

The frontend does **not** have an equivalent abstract `Service` interface. Instead, markdown rendering is handled concretely by:

- **`MemoMarkdownRenderer`** component at `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoContent/MemoMarkdownRenderer.tsx` line 56 -- wraps `react-markdown` with remark/rehype plugin chains and custom component overrides.
- **`MemoContent`** component at `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoContent/index.tsx` line 12 -- consumes `MemoMarkdownRenderer`.
- **`EditorController`** interface at `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/types/editorController.ts` line 8 -- an abstraction for the editor that exposes `getMarkdown()`, `setMarkdown()`, and `insertMarkdown()` methods. This is the closest to a TypeScript-side markdown processing interface, but it governs editor operations rather than rendering/parsing.
- **`MarkdownRenderContext`** at `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoContent/MarkdownRenderContext.tsx` -- a React context tracking nesting depth during rendering (not a processing interface).
- **Type definitions** at `/bench/repo/web/src/types/markdown.ts` -- interfaces for `TagNode`, `MentionNode`, etc. (data types, not processing abstractions).

---

### Summary

The repository has **one** formal markdown processing interface: `markdown.Service` in Go (`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`), with **one** concrete implementation (`service` struct, same file line 58), constructed via `markdown.NewService()`. It is injected into three struct types (`APIV1Service`, `RSSService`, `Runner`) and used across the API, RSS, webhook, and memo-payload-rebuild code paths. The frontend has no parallel abstraction -- it uses `react-markdown` directly through the `MemoMarkdownRenderer` component.
